title: Mount Kirkpatrick, Antarctica: Cryolophosaurus and the Hanson Formation
summary: A quarry near the base of the Hanson Formation, about 4,100 metres up Mount Kirkpatrick in the Central Transantarctic Mountains, yielded Cryolophosaurus ellioti, a crested theropod, with a basal sauropodomorph, a tritylodont tooth and a pterosaur bone. The siltstones and volcanic tuffs are Early Jurassic, and their age is poorly constrained, roughly 186 million years ago, or Sinemurian–Pliensbachian.

uncertainty.note: The Hanson Formation's age is 'not well constrained' (Elliot et al. 2007): Rb-Sr 186 ± 8 Ma on tuffs from Mt Falla, overlain by Ferrar rocks of 183.6 ± 1.8 Ma. The dinosaur is assigned a Sinemurian–Pliensbachian age by biostratigraphy. The start (194 Ma) is the top of the Rb-Sr range and the end (182 Ma) is the Ferrar age less its error; neither is a direct date on the quarry.

beats.caption: Silt, volcanic ash and tuffaceous sand built the Hanson Formation across the Beardmore Glacier region in the Early Jurassic.
A quarry near the formation base on Mount Kirkpatrick produced Cryolophosaurus ellioti, a nearly complete crested theropod.
These are the only known Early Jurassic dinosaurs from Antarctica, and fit a pattern of similar dinosaur faunas across Early Jurassic continents.
